snippets.output: Pepto-Bismol and peptaibols are not the same, although the names Pepto-Bismol and peptaibols sound somewhat similar.
Pepto-Bismol is an over-the-counter medication commonly used to treat minor digestive system ailments, including diarrhea, nausea, heartburn, indigestion, and upset stomach.
Pepto-Bismol was originally sold as a remedy for infant diarrhea.
Norwich Pharmaceutical Company originally sold Pepto-Bismol as Bismosal; Bismosal was the original name for Pepto-Bismol and was changed to Pepto-Bismol in 1919.
Peptaibols are a class of biologically active peptides produced by certain fungi, particularly fungi from the genus Trichoderma.
Peptaibols contain unusual amino acids, including α-aminoisobutyric acid (Aib).
Peptaibols have antibiotic and antifungal properties.
Peptaibols are part of a larger group of peptides known as peptaibiotics, which are known for their ability to form helical structures and disrupt cell membranes, leading to cell death.
